text:
alex: Heads up — I'm putting together a plan to reconcile the new metric_index naming and the console's read queries. We renamed route_metric -> route_metrics_idx in the ingest pipeline last week and console queries are starting to fail in canaries.

maya: ack. saw a handful of 500s on canary/region-us-west. quick question — are we planning a DB rename or a shadow-copy backfill? :eyes:

alex: Prefer minimal downtime. Proposal: 1) keep current column (route_metric) as alias for a rolling window; 2) write dual-writes for new rows to route_metrics_idx; 3) add a read adapter in the console that queries route_metrics_idx first, falls back to route_metric. Then run a batched backfill to populate old rows into the new column, and remove the alias after 30d.

jordan: sounds reasonable. do we have safe read semantics for mixed writes? concerned about double-counting in aggregation queries.

sre-carlos: double-counting is the main risk. We should ensure aggregations dedupe by primary key (route_id + ts) or by using the more precise metric_id. If we can't guarantee uniqueness, we might misreport quota usage.

maya: agreed. for quotas we need stable per-route numbers. If read adapter returns both columns we should coalesce in SQL: COALESCE(route_metrics_idx, route_metric). But dedupe on aggregates is better.

alex: here's the tentative SQL snippet for the read-adapter layer:  ```sql
  SELECT route_id, ts, COALESCE(route_metrics_idx.value, route_metric.value) AS value
  FROM metrics_view
  LEFT JOIN route_metrics_idx ON ...
  LEFT JOIN route_metric ON ...
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval '7 days';
  ```  This keeps queries simple while backfill runs.

emily: small nit: console dashboards use pre-aggregated rollups. We'll need to ensure rollup jobs read the adapter too, otherwise historical tiles will diverge. Who owns the rollup change? @ryan?

ryan: yep I can own the rollup change. Plan: update rollup workers to read from the same adapter layer, run in parallel for a week to compare deltas, then flip. I'll emit a delta report every 2h.

devops-bot: deploy accepted for feature/metric-index-read-adapter -> staging (sha: d4f2a1). Canaries scheduled.

jordan: operational concern — query plans. new JOINs might regress latency for long time ranges. Could we instead add a view that coalesces at ingestion time (materialized view) and have console read from that?

alex: good point. tradeoff: materialized view reduces read latency but increases storage and write latency. For canary load I'll start with non-materialized read-adapter + index hints, and if the p95 latency spikes we'll switch to a materialized view and synchronous refresh during off-peak.

maya: about the backfill: let's do chunked jobs by tenant range, idempotent upserts, and a safepoint so the backfill can be paused. We'll keep dual-write for 30 days after backfill completes for safety. Also add telemetry events for "backfill_progress" and a regression eval for dashboard numbers.

alex: noted. Telemetry plan: emit per-chunk metrics: rows_processed, rows_skipped, conflict_count, duration_ms. Hook into console telemetry so product can monitor drift.

ryan: for the quota system — we should compute user-facing quota numbers from the adapter so billable reporting is consistent. I'll coordinate with billing to ensure they read the adapter too.

jordan: acceptance tests? we should create synthetic traffic that exercises old+new columns and validate no double-counting at aggregate queries. Can also run smoke checks on console widgets.

alex: agreed. I'll add an integration test in the ingest suite that simulates dual-write and validates aggregates.

maya: timeline?

alex: proposed timeline: mock read-adapter today on staging; canary deploy tomorrow morning with 10% traffic; run canary 48h with delta reports; start backfill on day 3 in small chunks; full backfill ~3-4 days depending on throughput; cutover at day 10 if deltas < 1%.

emily: put a banner on the console dashboard during canary so internal users know numbers may wobble.

alex: will do. tagging follow-ups: @maya for backfill chunking, @ryan for rollup and quota, @jordan for query plans, @sre-carlos for canary SLOs. Any objections? :thumbsup:

jordan: :thumbsup: fine by me.

maya: +1

ryan: +1

sre-carlos: +1, will watch alerts.

alex: thanks team — I'll post the runbook after lunch and open the deployment PR.
